en: Getting behind the wheel of a car can be an exciting new step in a teen's life. But along with that excitement comes a new responsibility: understanding the need for common sense and maturity to avoid accidents. In an effort to spread awareness to teens across the nation, the Allstate Foundation sponsored a Keep the Drive summit at Sunset Station on January 23rd.
zh: 对青少年来说，坐上驾驶座、开始开车是人生中令人兴奋的新一步。但伴随这份兴奋而来的还有一份新的责任：要懂得常识与成熟心态对避免事故的必要性。为了向全国青少年普及安全意识，好事达基金会于1月23日在日落车站赞助举办了"安全驾驶"峰会。

en: An average of 16 teens die every day in motor vehicle crashes, and nearly 40% of those are caused by speeding. Texas is the state with the most teen driving deaths, according to the presentation. Students agreed that the statistics were amazing and made them think twice about how they drive.
zh: 平均每天有16名青少年死于机动车事故，其中近40%由超速造成。根据这份报告，得克萨斯州是青少年驾车死亡人数最多的州。学生们都认为这些统计数据令人震惊，也让他们重新审视自己的驾驶方式。

en: When you look at the list each morning, a big fat cloud of doom is right at the top — those difficult, complex, important tasks that are so crucial to get done and so easy to avoid. Plenty of us create a to-do list to address feelings of being overwhelmed, but we rarely use these tools to their best effect. They wind up being guilt-provoking reminders of the fact that we're overcommitted and losing control of our priorities.
zh: 每天早晨看一眼待办清单时，最上面总压着一大团"阴云"——那些既难又复杂、极其重要、非完成不可却最容易逃避的任务。我们很多人列待办清单是为了缓解被压得喘不过气的感受，却很少把这些工具用到最好。到头来，它们反倒成了让人内疚的提醒，提醒我们承诺过多、正在失去对优先事项的掌控。

en: The only thing neighbors have in common to begin with is proximity, and unless something more develops, that isn't reason enough to be best friends. It sometimes happens naturally, but the chances are very small that your neighbors will be your choice as friends, or that you will be theirs either. The best relationship with neighbors is one of friendly distance.
zh: 邻居之间一开始唯一的共同点就是住得近，如果之后没有更多的交集，这一点并不足以让彼此成为挚友。有时友谊确实会自然发生，但你的邻居正好成为你选择的朋友、或你成为他们选择的朋友，概率都非常小。与邻居最好的关系，是保持友好的距离。

en: I'm interested in the criminal justice system of our country. It seems to me that something has to be done if we're to survive as a country. I certainly don't know what the answers to our problems are. Things certainly get complicated in a hurry when you get into them. But I wonder if something couldn't be done to deal with some of these problems.
zh: 我对我们国家的刑事司法制度很感兴趣。在我看来，如果我们想让这个国家延续下去，就必须做点什么。我当然不知道我们这些问题的答案是什么，一旦深入进去，事情很快就会变得复杂。但我在想，是不是总可以做点什么来解决其中一些问题。

en: However, that does not mean that the person isn't guilty of the crime or that he shouldn't pay society the debt he owes. It's sad, of course, that a person may have to spend the rest of his life, or a large part of it, in prison for acts that he committed while not in full control of his mind.
zh: 然而，这并不意味着此人没有犯罪，也不意味着他不该偿还欠社会的债。当然，一个人可能因为心智并不完全清醒时所做的事，要在监狱里度过余生或大半辈子，这令人难过。

en: Every once in a while, the instructor makes a witty remark, causing others in the class to laugh. You smile politely, pretending that you've heard the remark and found it mildly humorous. You have a vague sense of guilt that you aren't paying close attention, but you tell yourself that any material you miss can be picked up from a friend's notes. Besides, the instructor is talking about road construction in Ancient Rome and nothing could be more boring.
zh: 每隔一会儿，老师会冒出一句俏皮话，引得班上其他人发笑。你礼貌地微笑，假装听见了那句话并觉得有点好笑。你隐约有些内疚，觉得自己没有专心听讲，但又安慰自己：漏掉的内容可以从朋友的笔记里补回来。再说，老师正在讲古罗马的道路建设，实在没有比这更无聊的了。

en: What else do we know about sensation seekers? Well, as I said, sensation seekers like strong emotions. You can see this trait in many parts of a person's life, not just in extreme sports. For example, many sensation seekers enjoy hard rock music; they like the loud sound and strong emotion of the songs. Similarly, sensation seekers enjoy frightening horror movies; they like the feeling of being scared and horrified while watching the movie.
zh: 关于"感觉寻求者"，我们还知道些什么？正如我说过的，感觉寻求者喜欢强烈的情绪。这种特质会体现在一个人生活的许多方面，而不只是极限运动。比如，很多感觉寻求者喜欢硬摇滚乐，他们喜欢歌曲里响亮的声音和浓烈的情绪。同样，他们也爱看吓人的恐怖片，享受观影时被惊吓、被震骇的感觉。

en: The new year always brings with it a cultural tradition of new possibilities. We see it as a chance for renewal. We begin to dream of new possible selves; we design our ideal self or an image that is quite different from what we are now. For some of us, we roll that dreamy film in our heads just because it's the beginning of a new year.
zh: 新年总会带来一种"新的可能"的文化传统。我们把它看作一次重新开始的机会，开始憧憬新的可能的自我，设计理想中的自己，或一个与当下截然不同的形象。对我们中的一些人来说，仅仅因为新的一年开始了，就会在脑海里播放那部充满幻想的影片。

en: Esperanto is an artificial language designed to serve internationally as an auxiliary means of communication among speakers of different languages. It was created by Ludwik Lejzer Zamenhof, a Polish Jewish doctor specializing in eye diseases. Esperanto was first presented in 1887. An international movement was launched to promote its use. Despite arguments and disagreements, the movement has continued to flourish and has members in more than 80 countries.
zh: 世界语是一种人造语言，旨在作为不同母语者之间的国际辅助交际工具。它由波兰犹太裔眼科医生路德维克·莱伊泽·柴门霍夫创造，1887年首次问世，随后兴起了一场推广使用的国际运动。尽管争论与分歧不断，这场运动仍持续蓬勃发展，在80多个国家都有成员。

en: It is taught in universities and used in many translations, often in scientific or technological works. El Popola Ĉinio, which means "From People's China," is a monthly magazine in Esperanto and is read worldwide. Radio Beijing's Esperanto program is the most popular program in Esperanto in the world. Esperanto's vocabulary is drawn primarily from Latin, the Romance languages, English and German. Spelling is completely regular. A simple and consistent set of endings indicates grammatical functions of words.
zh: 它在大学里被教授，也被用于大量译作，常见于科技类著作。《来自人民中国》是一份世界语月刊，在全球发行；北京电台的世界语节目是世界上最受欢迎的世界语节目。世界语词汇主要取自拉丁语、罗曼语族、英语和德语，拼写完全规则，一套简单一致的词尾即可表示词的语法功能。

en: You develop in-depth knowledge of the intricate structure of the language. Why do some non-native speakers of English claim that it's a difficult language to learn, while infants born into English-speaking communities acquire their language before they learn to use forks and knives? At the University of Sussex you are introduced to the nature and grammar of English in all its aspects.
zh: 你会深入掌握这门语言精妙的结构。为什么有些非英语母语者声称英语难学，而生在英语社区的婴儿却在学会用刀叉之前就掌握了母语？在萨塞克斯大学，你将从各个层面系统了解英语的本质与语法。

en: Articles in magazines and newspapers and special reports on radio and television reflect the concern of many Americans about the increasing dropout rate in our junior and senior high schools. Coupled with this fact is the warning that soon we will no longer have a workforce to fill the many jobs that require properly educated personnel. The high student dropout rate is not a recent development. 10 years ago, many urban schools were reporting dropout rates between 35 and 50%.
zh: 报刊文章和广播电视的专题报道，反映出许多美国人对初高中辍学率上升的担忧。与之相伴的警告是：我们很快将没有足够的劳动力去填补那些需要受过良好教育者才能胜任的岗位。高辍学率并非新近出现的问题，10年前，许多城市学校报告的辍学率就在35%到50%之间。

en: More than 50 years ago, the United Nations declared that literacy is a basic human right. It's very important for improving the lives of individuals. However, it is estimated that 880 million adults around the world are illiterate—that is, they are unable to read or write. A majority of them are women. More than 110 million school-aged children in the world do not attend school.
zh: 50多年前，联合国宣布识字是一项基本人权，它对改善个人生活极为重要。然而据估计，全球有8.8亿成年人是文盲，也就是不会读也不会写，其中大多数是女性。全世界还有超过1.1亿学龄儿童没有上学。

en: The third group has letters that are partly written below the lower line. John Morgan taught his students to write simple words from the letters. In this way, his students learnt more than 700 words. Many of them can now write to family members. They also can read newspapers and magazines.
zh: 第三组字母有一部分写在下线以下。约翰·摩根教学生用这些字母拼写简单的单词，就这样，学生们学会了700多个词。他们中许多人现在能给家人写信，也能读报纸和杂志了。

en: " Figuring out how humans acquire language may shed light on why some children learn to read and write later than others, Schafer says, and could lead to better treatments for developmental problems. What's more, the study of language acquisition offers direct insight into how humans learn. "Language is a test case for human cognitive development," says Schafer.
zh: 谢弗说，弄清人类如何习得语言，或许能解释为什么有些孩子学会读写比别人晚，并可能为发育问题带来更好的干预办法。更重要的是，语言习得研究能直接揭示人类是如何学习的。他说："语言是检验人类认知发展的一块试金石。"

en: Thus, how we see ourselves reflects the views of us that others communicate. The profound connection between identity and communication is dramatically evident in children who are deprived of human contact. Case studies of children who were isolated from others reveal that they lack a firm self-concept, and their mental and psychological development is severely hindered by lack of language. Communication with others not only affects our sense of identity, but also directly influences our physical and emotional well-being.
zh: 因此，我们如何看待自己，反映的是他人传递给我们的看法。身份认同与交往之间的深刻联系，在被剥夺人际交往的儿童身上表现得最为明显。对被隔离儿童的个案研究显示，他们缺乏稳固的自我概念，其心智与心理发展也因缺少语言而严重受阻。与他人交往不仅影响我们的身份感，还直接左右我们的身体与情绪健康。

en: The Ancient Greeks developed basic memory systems called mnemonics. The name is derived from their goddess of memory, Mnemosyne. In the ancient world, a trained memory was an immense asset, particularly in public life. There were no convenient devices for taking notes, and early Greek orators delivered long speeches with great accuracy because they learned the speeches using mnemonic systems. The Greeks discovered that human memory is largely an associative process—that it works by linking things together.
zh: 古希腊人发展出被称为"记忆术"的基础记忆系统，名称源自他们的记忆女神谟涅摩绪涅。在古代，训练有素的记忆力是一笔巨大财富，尤其在公共生活中：当时没有便于记笔记的工具，而早期希腊演说家却能极准确地发表长篇演说，因为他们用记忆术记住了讲稿。希腊人发现，人的记忆本质上是一个联想过程——靠把事物联系起来运作。

en: If you remember the shape of Italy, it is because you have been told some time that Italy is shaped like a boot. You made an association with something already known. The shape of a boot and the shape of Italy could not be forgotten once you had made the association.
zh: 你之所以记得意大利的形状，是因为有人曾告诉你意大利像一只靴子。你把它与已知的事物建立了联想。一旦形成这种联想，靴子的形状和意大利的轮廓就再也忘不掉了。

en: He runs an organization that checks out products for consumers. The scientists hired to design the scents disagree. "There's soft background music, there's special lighting, there are all sorts of bells being used," says Dr. Hirsch. "Why not smells? " One reason why not, says Silbergeld, is that some people are allergic to certain scents pumped into products or stores. But there's a whole other side to this debate: do the smells really work?
zh: 他经营着一家为消费者检测产品的机构。受聘设计气味的科学家们却持不同意见。赫希博士说："有柔和的背景音乐，有特别的灯光，还有各种铃铛被用上，为什么不能用气味呢？"西尔伯格尔德认为不用的一个理由是：有些人对注入产品或商店的某些气味过敏。但这场争论还有另一面：这些气味真的有效吗？

en: But when the storm is brewing, the pressure drops and you are often able to see things more clearly. Sailors took note of this long ago and came up with the saying, "The farther the sight, the nearer the rain. " Your sense of smell can also help you detect weather changes. Just before it rains, odors become stronger. This is because odors are repressed in a fair high-pressure center.
zh: 但暴风雨将临之时，气压下降，你往往能把东西看得更清楚。水手们很早就注意到这一点，于是有了那句谚语："看得越远，雨来得越近。"嗅觉也能帮你察觉天气变化：下雨前气味会变浓，这是因为在晴朗的高压中心里，气味被压制住了。

en: One of the most common images of an advanced, western-style culture is that of a busy, traffic-filled city. Since their first appearance on American roadways, automobiles have become a symbol of progress, a source of thousands of jobs, and an almost inalienable right for citizens' personal freedom and movement. In recent decades, our love affair with the car is being exported directly to the developing world. And it is increasingly apparent that this transfer is leading to disaster.
zh: 提到先进的西式文化，最常见的画面之一便是繁忙拥挤、车流不息的城市。汽车自登上美国道路以来，一直是进步的象征、成千上万个就业岗位的来源，也几乎成了公民个人自由与出行不可剥夺的权利。近几十年来，我们对汽车的这份热爱正被直接输出到发展中国家，而这种转移正越来越明显地走向灾难。

en: Water scooters are water vehicles that look very much like motorcycles. Nowadays, speedy, colorful water scooters are gaining in popularity. They can travel anywhere a small boat can and are typically popular with young people. The rising popularity of the craft has raised the question of water scooter regulation. In this case, the argument for strict regulation is compelling. Water scooters are a particularly deadly form of water recreation. For example, two women were vacationing in Longboat Key.
zh: 水上摩托是一种外形酷似摩托车的水上交通工具。如今，速度快、颜色鲜艳的水上摩托越来越受欢迎，凡是小船能到的地方它都能去，尤其受年轻人青睐。它的走红引出了是否该加强监管的问题，而在这个问题上，主张严格监管的理由很有说服力：水上摩托是尤其致命的水上娱乐方式。例如，有两位女士正在长船礁度假。

en: Providing more water vehicles to compete for the same space in crowded waterways is simply an open invitation to disaster. In addition to the inherent operational hazards of water scooters, they are proven to be an environmental nuisance. Beach residents complain of the noise of the scooters. The Pacific Whale Foundation on the west coast expressed the concern that the scooters are frightening away an endangered species of whale that migrates to Hawaii for breeding.
zh: 在拥挤的水域里再增加更多争抢同一空间的交通工具，无异于公开招来灾难。除了水上摩托本身固有的操作危险，它还被证实是环境公害：海滩居民抱怨它的噪音；西海岸的太平洋鲸鱼基金会则担忧，它会吓跑一种迁徙到夏威夷繁殖的濒危鲸类。

en: If business people can choose between a three-hour train journey from city centre to city centre and a one-hour flight, they'll choose the train, says an executive travel consultant. They won't go by plane any more. If you calculate flight time, check-in and travel to and from the airport, you'll find almost no difference. And if your plane arrives late due to bad weather or air traffic jams or strikes, then the train passengers will arrive at their destination first.
zh: 一位商务旅行顾问说，如果商务人士能在"市中心到市中心三小时火车"和"一小时飞机"之间选择，他们会选火车，不再坐飞机了。把飞行时间、值机以及往返机场的路程都算进去，你会发现几乎没有差别。而如果飞机因恶劣天气、空中拥堵或罢工晚点，火车上的乘客反而会先到目的地。

en: Farmers usually use plows to prepare their fields for planting crops. Plows cut into the ground and lift up weeds and other unwanted plants. However, plowing is blamed for causing severe damage to topsoil by removing the plants that protect the soil from being blown or washed away. Many farmers in South Asia are now trying a process called low-till farming. Low-till farming limits the use of plows.
zh: 农民通常用犁来整地备耕，犁翻开土壤、把杂草和其他无用植物翻出来。但犁耕被指责会严重破坏表土，因为它清掉了保护土壤不被风吹走、被水冲走的植被。如今南亚许多农民在尝试一种叫"少耕"的做法，少耕会限制犁的使用。

en: Farmers grow rice during wet weather. During the dry season, they grow wheat in the same fields. Farmers are using the low-till method to plant wheat after harvesting rice. Scientists say low-till agriculture is one of the best examples in the world of technologies working for both people and the environment.
zh: 农民在雨季种水稻，旱季则在同一块地里种小麦。他们用少耕法在收完水稻后直接播下小麦。科学家说，少耕农业是世界上"技术同时造福人与环境"的最佳范例之一。

en: If such an earthquake happened today, it would be felt from the Rocky Mountains to the Atlantic Ocean and would flatten most of the cities in the Mississippi Valley. That, he figured, should get his classmates' attention. Throughout the body of the speech, Juan dealt only with the basic mechanics of earthquakes and carefully avoided technical terms. He also prepared visual aids, diagramming fault lines so his classmates wouldn't get confused.
zh: 他推算，若这样的地震发生在今天，从落基山脉到大西洋沿岸都能感觉到，密西西比河谷的大多数城市会被夷平——这总该能抓住同学们的注意力了。整篇演讲里，胡安只讲地震的基本原理，刻意避开专业术语；他还准备了直观教具，把断层线画成图，免得同学们听糊涂。

en: Wilma Subra had no intention of becoming a public speaker. After graduating from college with degrees in chemistry and microbiology, she went to work at Gulf South Research Institute in Louisiana. As part of her job, she conducted field research on toxic substances in the environment, often in minority communities located near large industrial polluters. She found many families were being exposed to high, sometimes deadly levels of chemicals and other toxic substances.
zh: 威尔玛·苏布拉从没想过要成为公众演说家。大学拿到化学与微生物学学位后，她进入路易斯安那州的墨西哥湾南方研究所工作。工作的一部分是在环境中做有毒物质的实地研究，地点常是大型污染企业附近的少数族裔社区。她发现许多家庭正暴露在高浓度、有时甚至致命的化学物质和其他有毒物中。

en: 25 years ago, Ray Anderson, a single parent with a one-year-old son, witnessed a terrible accident. It took place when the driver of a truck ran a red light and collided with the car of Sandra Jenkins. The impact of the collision killed Sandra instantly, but her three-month-old daughter was left trapped in the burning car.
zh: 25年前，带着一岁儿子的单亲父亲雷·安德森目睹了一场可怕的事故：一辆卡车司机闯红灯，撞上了桑德拉·詹金斯的汽车。撞击让桑德拉当场身亡，而她三个月大的女儿被困在起火的汽车里。

en: His son was soon adopted by relatives. The most remarkable part of the story unfolded only last week. Karen and her boyfriend Michael were looking through some old boxes when they came across some old newspaper clippings. "This is me when I was a newborn baby. I was rescued from a burning car, but my mother died in the accident," explained Karen.
zh: 他的儿子很快被亲戚收养。这个故事最令人称奇的部分直到上周才揭开：凯伦和男友迈克尔翻一些旧箱子时，翻出了几张旧剪报。"这是刚出生时的我，我从着火的汽车里被救出来，可妈妈在那场事故里去世了，"凯伦解释道。

en: He was a good student, but he liked to drink alcohol and play card games for money. As an unskilled game player, he often lost money. Since he couldn't pay his gambling losses, he left the university and began working for magazines. He worked hard, yet he was not well paid or well known. At the age of 27, he got married.
zh: 他是个好学生，却爱喝酒、玩牌赌钱。作为不熟练的玩家，他常输钱；因为付不起赌债，他离开大学，开始给杂志社打工。他工作努力，却既没拿到好报酬，也没出名。27岁那年，他结了婚。

en: Some critics say Poe was one of America's best writers and even had a great influence on many French writers. But others disagree. They say Poe's work is difficult to understand and most of his writing describes very unpleasant situations and events. Edgar Allan Poe died in 1849 when he was 40 years old. It is said that he was found dead after days of heavy drinking.
zh: 有些评论家说坡是美国最优秀的作家之一，甚至对许多法国作家影响深远；也有人不同意，认为坡的作品难懂，且大多描写极不愉快的情境与事件。埃德加·爱伦·坡1849年去世，年仅40岁。据说他是在连日酗酒后被人发现死亡的。

en: It is important to point out that students also need to have a deep understanding of their own culture before they can begin to observe, analyze, and evaluate other cultures. In multicultural societies, people can study each other's cultures to develop intercultural competencies such as critical and reflective thinking and intellectual flexibility. This can be done both through the curriculum and through activities on campus outside of the classroom, such as art exhibitions and lectures from international experts.
zh: 需要指出的是，学生在开始观察、分析和评价其他文化之前，也得对本国文化有深刻理解。在多元文化社会里，人们可以通过研究彼此的文化来培养跨文化交流能力，比如批判性与反思性思维、智识上的灵活性。这既可以通过课程实现，也能借助课堂之外的校园活动，如艺术展和国际专家讲座。

en: With brown hair, the woman was rated more capable, and she was offered a higher salary than when she had golden or red hair. Other studies have found similar results. Many respondents rate women with golden hair as less intelligent than other people, and redheads as more temperamental. Women with red or golden hair are victims of the common practice of stereotyping. A stereotype is a simplistic or exaggerated image that humans carry in their minds about groups of people.
zh: 换成棕发时，这位女性被认为更能干，拿到的薪水也比金发或红发时更高。其他研究也得到类似结果：许多受访者觉得金发女性不如别人聪明，红发女性则脾气更急躁。红发或金发女性是刻板印象这一普遍做法的受害者；刻板印象是人脑中对某类人持有的简单化或夸大的形象。

en: Between 1969 and 1989, employed Americans added an average of 138 hours to their yearly work schedules. The workweek has remained at above 40 hours, but people are working more weeks each year. Specifically, paid time off—holidays, vacations, sick leave—shrank by 50% in the 1980s, as corporations have experienced stiff competition and slower growth in productivity. They have pressed employees to work longer.
zh: 1969到1989年间，美国在职者平均每年多工作138小时。每周工时仍保持在40小时以上，但人们一年里工作的周数变多了。具体看，带薪休假——节假日、年假、病假——在80年代缩水了50%，因为企业面临激烈竞争、生产率增长放缓，于是迫使员工延长工作时间。

en: In many stressful situations, the body's responses can improve our performance. We become more energetic, more alert, better able to take effective action. But when stress is encountered continually, the body's reactions are more likely to be harmful than helpful to us. The continual speeding up of bodily reactions and the production of stress-related hormones seem to make people more susceptible to heart disease.
zh: 在许多紧张情境下，身体的反应能提升我们的表现：我们更有精力、更警觉，也更能采取有效行动。但当压力持续不断出现时，身体的反应更可能有害而非有益。身体反应持续加速、应激相关激素不断分泌，似乎会让人更容易患上心脏病。

en: Western doctors are beginning to understand what traditional healers have always known: that the body and the mind are inseparable. Until recently, modern urban physicians healed the body, psychiatrists the mind, and priests the soul. However, the medical world is now paying more attention to holistic medicine, which is an approach based on the belief that people's state of mind can make them sick or speed their recovery from sickness.
zh: 西方医生开始理解传统医者一直明白的道理：身体与心灵不可分割。直到不久前，现代城市里的内科医生治身体，精神科医生治心智，牧师照管灵魂。而如今医学界正越来越重视整体医学——这种路径基于一个信念：人的心理状态既能让人生病，也能加快病后康复。

en: Surprisingly, more patients in the second group showed the desired effect than those in the first group. In study after study, there is a positive reaction in almost one-third of the patients taking harmless substances. How is this possible? How can such a substance have an effect on the body? Evidence from a study at the University of California shows that several patients who received such substances were able to produce their own natural drug.
zh: 出人意料的是，第二组中出现预期效果的患者比第一组更多。一项又一项研究显示，服用无害物质的患者里，几乎有三分之一出现阳性反应。这怎么可能？这样的物质又怎能对身体产生作用？加州大学一项研究的证据表明，几名服用此类物质的患者能够自己产生天然的"药物"。

en: It is sometimes required that we work overtime and that we change shifts four or five times a month. That disturbs our personal lives, disrupts our sleeping and eating habits, and isolates us from everything except job-related friends and activities. The quality of nursing care is being affected dramatically by these situations. Most hospitals are now staffed by new graduates, as experienced nurses finally give up trying to change the system.
zh: 有时我们被要求加班，一个月还要换四五次班。这打乱了私人生活，破坏了睡眠和饮食习惯，也把我们与工作相关的朋友和活动之外的一切隔离开来。护理质量正被这些状况严重影响。如今大多数医院由刚毕业的新手撑着，因为有经验的护士终于放弃去改变这套体制了。

en:
— Hey, Steve. Do you happen to know where the movie theater is downtown?
— The one near the hospital?
— Yeah.
— Why do you want to know?
— Well, you know Jennifer, my cousin? She is newly in town. On Monday I asked her out on a date for this coming Saturday night.
— Wow, sounds great. Okay, write down these directions so you don't get lost.
— Okay, go ahead.
zh: ——嗨，史蒂夫，你知不知道市中心那家电影院在哪儿？——医院旁边那家？——对。——你问这个干嘛？——嗯，你认识我表妹詹妮弗吧？她刚到城里。周一我约了她这周六晚上出去约会。——哇，挺好。来，把这些路线记下来，别迷路。——好，你说。

en:
You'll see a parking lot on the left side of the street. Okay so far?
— Okay, then what?
— Then turn left on Third Street and drive east. The Pink Flamingo is the building just before the river on the left side. I think it's open weekdays from 10:30 in the morning to 11:30 at night. But it stays open until midnight on the weekends.
— Okay, I think I've driven by there before. Oh, last thing.
zh: 你会看到街左边有个停车场，到目前还清楚吗？——清楚，然后呢？——然后在第三街左转往东开。"粉红火烈鸟"就是河边左侧、快到河之前那栋楼。我想它工作日从上午10点半开到晚上11点半，周末会开到午夜。——好，我好像以前开车路过那儿。哦，还有最后一件事。

en:
— Hi Tim, I'm really sorry to hear about your dad. My sincerest condolences go out to you and your family. He was such a great man.
— Thanks. As you know, he had been sick for some time before he passed away, so we were somewhat prepared.
— So how's your mom taking it?
— Oh, it's been really hard on her. I don't think you get over something like that.
— Yeah, I'm sure. My heart really goes out to her.
zh: ——嗨，蒂姆，听说你父亲的事我很难过，向你和全家致以最诚挚的慰问，他是位很好的人。——谢谢。你也知道，他走之前病了一段时间，所以我们多少有些准备。——那你妈妈现在怎么样？——唉，她真的很难熬，我觉得这种事是过不去的。——是啊，我完全能理解，真的很心疼她。

en:
— Well, some of the family members will get together on Tuesday morning for a private memorial service. But there will be a viewing in the afternoon from two o'clock to three o'clock, followed by the funeral service. One of my uncles will be giving the eulogy.
— I wish there was something I could do.
— Well, actually there is.
zh: ——嗯，周二上午部分家人会聚一下，办个私人的追思仪式；下午两点到三点有瞻仰遗容，之后是葬礼，由我一位叔叔致悼词。——真希望我能帮上点什么。——其实还真有。

en:
— Hi Mary, do you want to start writing a lab report after we finish this experiment?
— I can't. In fact I need to finish early because I'm going over to the psychology department to talk to Professor Smith about a job opening.
— You mean a job on campus?
— Yeah, and it sounds pretty interesting. It involves helping with her study on learning styles.
zh: ——嗨，玛丽，做完这个实验后要不要开始写实验报告？——不行，其实我得早点结束，因为我要去心理系找史密斯教授谈一个职位空缺。——你是说校内的岗位？——对，听起来还挺有意思，是帮她做关于学习风格的研究。

en:
Now will you mostly do the testing or the tutoring?
— Both, I hope. I want to be involved from start to finish.
— Are you getting paid for this?
— I'm sure we'll get something, though probably not much. Anyway, it doesn't matter to me, I just want to have some hands-on experience.
— Yeah, and it'll be nice to help those high school students too.
— That's what I thought when I saw the ad, you know. You could do it too.
zh: 那你主要做测试还是做辅导？——我希望两头都参与，想从头跟到尾。——这个有报酬吗？——应该会有一点，不过大概不多。反正对我来说无所谓，我只是想有点实操经验。——是啊，而且能帮到那些高中生也挺好的。——我看到广告时就是这么想的，你也可以去试试。

en:
When I tried to register three weeks ago, she said I just had to pay a late fee.
— She must have been a temporary worker. They don't have much training. Why didn't you register then?
— She said I couldn't until I had my birth certificate. Here it is.
— Your birth certificate?
— Well, I'm a new part-time student, so she asked for identification. I don't drive, so I don't have a driver's license.
— That's no reason to demand a birth certificate.
zh: 三周前我去注册时，她说我只要交一笔滞纳金就行。——她肯定是临时工，没受过多少培训。那你当时怎么没注册成？——她说得等我拿到出生证明才行。这不，带来了。——出生证明？——嗯，我是新来的非全日制学生，所以她要我出示身份证明。我不开车，没有驾照。——那也不该非要出生证明啊。

en:
We only need to establish residency. A phone bill with your name and address on it would have been fine.
— Really? Only proof of my address?
— Yes. I'm afraid she gave you the wrong information. Still, you'll have to wait and take your maths class next semester.
— But that's unfair.
— Well, I sympathize with your problem, but frankly, I don't think there is anything anyone can do for you. You were trapped in the system.
zh: 我们只需要确认居住地址，一张写有你姓名和地址的电话账单就足够了。——真的？只要能证明地址就行？——是的，恐怕她给了你错误的信息。不过你还是得等，数学课只能下学期再修了。——可这不公平。——我理解你的难处，但坦白说，我觉得谁也帮不了你，你是被这套流程卡住了。

en:
— Well, I went to the registration to get my transcript, but they said there are some outstanding fines that I have to settle before they can release it.
— Then just pay the fine and you can get your transcript. What's the big problem?
— Yeah, that's exactly what I thought, but the fine came to 150 dollars and that was a shock to me.
— Oh, that's a bit of a bite. Did you keep the book for long?
— Guess what?
zh: ——嗯，我去注册处拿成绩单，可他们说有几笔未结清的罚款，得先缴清才能发。——那就把罚款交了，成绩单不就拿到了，有什么大不了的？——是啊，我本来也这么想，可罚款一共150美元，把我吓了一跳。——哦，这确实有点咬人。书你借了很久吗？——你猜怎么着？

en:
— Excuse me, may I have some information about the reception party that you are advertising outside? It's for new students, isn't that right?
— That's right. And what would you like to know about it?
— Well, I'm not really sure what the purpose of the event is.
— The party will provide students with a chance to get to know each other, and a chance for students who have successfully been through university to pass on some valuable advice.
zh: ——打扰一下，我想问问外面广告上那个迎新招待会，是给新生办的吧？——没错，你想了解哪方面？——嗯，我不太清楚这个活动的目的是什么。——这个招待会能让同学们互相认识，也让顺利读完大学的学长学姐传授一些宝贵的经验。

en:
— Who is organizing the event? Is it the faculty, or actually the alumni association?
— It is the alumni association. So it's strictly a student-to-student event.
— I hope we won't have to sit through a lot of boring speeches. I mean, aren't these students just brains anyway? What can they actually do to help a guy like me?
— No, these people are not brains at all.
zh: ——谁在组织这个活动？是院系，还是校友会？——是校友会，所以严格说完全是学生对学生。——希望不用坐着听一大堆无聊的演讲。我是说，那些人不就是些书呆子吗？对我这样的人能有什么实际帮助？——不，这些人根本不是书呆子。

en:
Those are, after all, success stories if they've managed to survive university life. I hear about only half of all students who start university actually finish it.
— And besides that, there's another reason to go.
— What's that?
— The pie they'll be serving is delicious. I know it, since I'm the one who will be making it.
zh: 毕竟能顺利熬过大学生活本身就是成功案例。我听说所有入学的人里只有大约一半最后能毕业。——而且去那儿还有另一个理由。——什么理由？——现场供应的派特别好吃。我知道，因为是我做的。

en:
— Hi Wendy, only two more weeks of classes.
— Eight school days actually. Then exams start.
— Yes, then I will be glad when exams are over.
— What are you doing for the summer break?
— I would like to go to Italy and work at a restaurant in Florence. My uncle owns a restaurant specializing in seafood, and he has offered me a casual job.
— That would be a wonderful summer.
zh: ——嗨，温迪，只剩两周课了。——其实只剩八个上课日，然后就考试了。——是啊，考完我就解放了。——暑假你打算做什么？——我想去意大利，在佛罗伦萨一家餐馆打工。我叔叔开着一家专做海鲜的餐厅，他给我留了个临时岗位。——那会是个很棒的夏天。

en:
I would love to go to Nepal as a volunteer to instruct local residents in engineering skills. It would be a chance to share what you already know.
— However?
— I don't find out until next week whether or not I've been accepted into the program. If I do get accepted, I won't be making any money, and I need money to return to university for my final year in September.
— I can see your problem.
zh: 我很想去尼泊尔做志愿者，教当地居民工程技术，也是个把自己已有的知识分享出去的机会。——不过呢？——要到下周我才知道有没有被项目录取。就算录取了也赚不到钱，而我九月回学校读最后一年是需要钱的。——我明白你的难处了。

en:
And they often ask what makes me decide to join their company, especially when they are rather small and young.
— You can tell them that you believe you would have better opportunities with a small but rapidly expanding company like theirs.
— Great. I think the most difficult question is what my greatest strengths and weaknesses are.
— They are tough questions.
zh: 他们还常问我，是什么让我决定加入他们公司，尤其公司规模还小、成立又没多久。——你可以告诉他们，你相信在像他们这样规模不大但扩张很快的公司里，机会会更好。——好主意。我觉得最难的问题是"我最大的优点和缺点是什么"。——这两问确实不好答。

en:
For your greatest strengths, give a response like this: I can see what needs to be done and do it, or I work well with others.
— Terrific.
— For your weaknesses, you can identify one or two, such as "I tend to drive myself too hard. " The trick is to describe a weakness so that it could also be considered a virtue.
— I see. Sometimes they also ask me what I don't like about my previous jobs.
zh: 说最大优点时，可以这么答："我能看出该做什么并把它做好"，或者"我善于与人合作"。——太棒了。——说缺点时，可以挑一两个，比如"我往往把自己逼得太紧"。诀窍是把缺点说得同时也可以被看成一种优点。——明白了。有时他们还会问我不喜欢上一份工作的哪些方面。

en:
— Good morning, class.
— Good morning, sir.
— Today we'll discuss volcanoes. Can you tell me the most dangerous thing about a volcano?
— I think the most dangerous hazard of a volcano comes from the lava that flows out of it.
— Good guess. Although your answer makes sense, the biggest killer from a volcano comes from the ash, not the lava. In fact, ash causes serious problems and can make humans and animals sick. It can even kill them.
zh: ——同学们早上好。——老师早上好。——今天我们来讨论火山。谁能告诉我火山最危险的是什么？——我觉得火山最危险的危害来自流出来的熔岩。——猜得不错。虽然你的答案说得通，但火山最大的杀手是火山灰，不是熔岩。事实上，火山灰会引发严重问题，能让人和动物生病，甚至致死。

en:
Ash also reduces sunlight and can start heavy rainfalls that lead to mudslides. Did you know that it only takes 30 centimeters of dry ash to collapse a roof of a building? Ash also contaminates water supplies and kills crops. As you can see, ash causes the most destruction.
— Professor, are there different sizes of volcanoes?
— Absolutely.
zh: 火山灰还会遮挡阳光，并可能带来强降雨、引发泥石流。你知道吗，只要30厘米厚的干灰就能压塌房顶。它还会污染水源、毁掉庄稼。可见火山灰造成的破坏最大。——教授，火山有不同规模吗？——当然有。

en:
Super volcanoes are quite rare, with the last eruption occurring about 74,000 years ago in Indonesia.
— How do super volcanoes differ from ordinary volcanoes, and are they easy to find?
— By and large, most people would not be able to recognize a super volcano. Like an iceberg, the larger part of the volcano is hidden.
— Professor, if the volcano hasn't erupted, then how do scientists know what might happen?
zh: 超级火山非常罕见，上一次喷发大约在7.4万年前的印度尼西亚。——超级火山和普通火山有什么不同，容易发现吗？——大体上说，多数人认不出超级火山。它像冰山一样，更大的部分藏在下面。——教授，如果火山还没喷发，科学家怎么知道可能会发生什么？

en:
— You already have me walking about five blocks. Are you sure it is only a five-minute walk?
— Maybe it is longer? Actually, it could be more like 10 minutes, I am not sure.
— Do you know if there is a bus stop there?
— Yes, the bus stop is in front of the pool, but bus service is quite slow during the day.
— Are the tennis courts in good condition?
— Yes, this university is very lucky to have such sports facilities.
zh: ——你已经让我走了差不多五个街区了，你确定只要走五分钟？——也许更久？其实可能差不多十分钟，我也不确定。——你知道那边有没有公交站吗？——有，站就在游泳池前面，不过白天公交很慢。——网球场状况好吗？——很好，这所大学能有这样的体育设施真是很幸运。

en:
— That's what I've heard. Did a rich person donate some money?
— Yes, about five or six years ago. The rumor is that a famous hockey player left millions of dollars to build a new sports complex. It was an anonymous donation. Actually, I'm sorry to say I almost never used it. After my first year, besides studying, I took up cards. I love playing bridge.
— Well, I hope to get in good shape here.
zh: ——我也是这么听说的。是有钱人捐了款吗？——对，大概五六年前。传言说一位著名冰球运动员留下几百万美元建了新的体育中心，是匿名捐赠。不过说来惭愧，我几乎没怎么用过。大一一过，除了学习我还迷上了打牌，特别爱打桥牌。——嗯，我倒是希望在这儿把身体练好。

en:
He wasn't there long, though, because his mother passed away just four years later. Jimmy's father sent him back to Indiana after that to live with his aunt.
— So how did he get into acting?
— Well, first he acted in plays at high school. Then he went to college in California, where he got seriously into acting. In 1951 he moved to New York to do more stage acting.
— Then when did his movie career really start?
— 1955.
zh: 不过他在那儿没待多久，因为四年后母亲就去世了，之后吉米的父亲把他送回印第安纳，跟姑妈一起住。——那他是怎么走上表演这条路的？——嗯，起初在高中演戏，后来去加州上大学，在那儿真正认真做起表演。1951年他搬到纽约，演了更多舞台剧。——那他的电影生涯真正始于什么时候？——1955年。

en:
— Mr. Stern, may I ask you, do you think it was necessary and fair to arrest Steve Brill?
— I don't know whether you realize that this man has been eating up our park for five years, and he is encouraging other people to do the same thing every single day. He's been organizing groups to destroy our urban wildlife.
— But Mr. Stern, this situation has been going on happily for five years.
zh: ——斯特恩先生，能请教一下，您认为逮捕史蒂夫·布里尔是必要且公正的吗？——我不知道你是否意识到，这个人五年来一直在"吃掉"我们的公园，而且每天都怂恿别人照做。他一直在组织团体破坏城市里的野生动植物。——可是斯特恩先生，这五年来一切相安无事啊。

en:
Why do you suddenly decide to do something about it?
— Well, at first we just thought he was an eccentric person, a bit odd, you know. But over the years we came to realize that he is a dangerous guy. He's been ruining our city environment. Parks are to look at, not to eat. It's just as if you're going to allow people to walk through a zoo and eat the baby bears.
zh: 为什么你们突然决定要管这件事？——嗯，起初我们只当他是个怪人，有点古怪，你知道的。但这些年下来我们逐渐意识到，他是个危险人物，一直在毁掉我们的城市环境。公园是用来看的，不是用来吃的。这就好比允许人们逛动物园时把小熊吃掉。

en:
— Can we make you an offer? We would like to run the campaign for four extra weeks.
— Well, can we summarize the problem from our point of view? First of all, the campaign was late — it missed two important trade fairs. The ads also did not appear in two key magazines. As a result, the campaign failed. Do you accept that summary of what happened?
— Well, the delay wasn't entirely our fault.
zh: ——我们能提个方案吗？我们想把宣传活动再延长四周。——嗯，能不能先从我们的角度把问题梳理一下？首先，这次活动晚了，错过了两场重要的贸易展会；广告也没能出现在两家关键杂志上，结果活动失败了。你认可这个经过的归纳吗？——嗯，延误也不全是我们的责任。

en:
You did in fact make late changes to the specifications of the advertisements.
— Hmm, actually, you were late with the initial proposals, so we had very little time. And in fact we only asked for small changes.
— Well, whatever. Can we repeat our offer to run the campaign for four extra weeks?
— That's not really the point. The campaign missed two key trade fairs.
zh: 广告的规格确实是你们后来才临时改的。——唔，其实是最初的提案你们交晚了，我们时间很紧，而且我们提的只是很小的改动。——好吧，先不说这些。我们能再提一次把活动延长四周的方案吗？——问题不在这儿，这次活动错过了两场关键展会。

en:
— You know, I've often wondered why people laugh at a picture of a big-bellied businessman slipping on a banana skin and falling on his bottom.
— We like to feel sorry for him.
— Actually, Laura, I think we laugh because we're glad it didn't happen to us. But of course, there's also a kind of humorous satisfaction in seeing somebody self-important making a fool of themselves.
— Yes.
zh: ——你知道吗，我一直纳闷，为什么人们看到一个大腹便便的商人踩到香蕉皮、一屁股摔在地上会笑。——我们大概是想同情他吧。——其实，劳拉，我觉得我们笑是因为庆幸这事没发生在自己身上。当然，看见一个自以为了不起的人出丑，也有一种带幽默感的快意。——是啊。

en:
— Oh, you know, all those old films where somebody gets so outraged with his boss, he picks up a custard pie and plasters it all over the other person's face?
— That never makes me laugh very much, because you can guess it's going to happen. But a lot of people still find it laughable. It must be because it's the sort of thing we'd all love to do once in a while and never quite have the courage to.
zh: ——哦，你知道那些老电影吧，有人被老板气坏了，抄起一盘蛋奶派整个糊到对方脸上？——这我倒不太觉得好笑，因为你早猜到要发生。可很多人还是觉得可笑。大概因为这种事我们偶尔都想干一次，却始终没那个胆子。

en:
— There is an element there about competition though, isn't there? Because British Railways is a nationalized industry, there's only one railway system in the country. If you don't like a particular can of baked beans, you can go and buy another, but if you don't like a particular railway, you can't go and use another.
— Some people who write to me say this.
zh: ——不过这里面也有竞争的因素，对吧？因为英国铁路是国有化行业，全国只有一套铁路系统。你不喜欢某罐焗豆，可以去买另一罐；可你不喜欢某条铁路，却没法改用另一条。——有些给我写信的人就是这么说的。

en:
Because in general, modes of transport are all around. Let's face the fact: the car arrived, the car is here to stay, there is no question about that.
— So what you're saying then is that if the railways hadn't been nationalized, they would simply have disappeared.
— Oh, I think they would have. They're disappearing fast in America. The French railways lose 1 billion pounds a year; the German railways, 2 billion pounds a year.
zh: 因为总体上交通方式到处都有。我们得正视事实：汽车来了，汽车会一直存在，这点毫无疑问。——那你的意思是，如果铁路当初没有国有化，早就消失了吧？——哦，我想是的。在美国它们正迅速消失；法国铁路一年亏10亿英镑，德国铁路一年亏20亿英镑。

en:
But you see, those governments are prepared to pour money into the transport system to keep it going.
— So in a sense, you cope between two extremes. On the one hand, you're trying not to lose too much money, and on the other hand, you've got to provide the best service.
— Yes, you're right.
zh: 但你要明白，那些政府愿意往交通系统里砸钱来维持运转。——所以某种意义上，你得在两个极端之间找平衡：一方面尽量别亏太多钱，另一方面又得提供最好的服务。——对，你说得没错。

en:
We didn't have them very often, but when we did, I needed to make sure they were well taken care of. After all, the customer is always right.
— That's how we feel here too. How long did you work there?
— I was there for three and a half years. I left the company last month.
— And why did you leave?
— My husband has been transferred to Boston, and I understand your company has an opening there too.
zh: 我们并不常有这样的客人，但一旦有，我就得确保他们被照顾周全。毕竟顾客永远是对的。——我们这儿也是这么想的。你在那儿干了多久？——三年半，上个月刚离职。——为什么离开？——我先生被调到了波士顿，我了解到贵公司在那边也有空缺。

en:
— Well, in the studio this morning for our interview spot is Peter Wilson. Peter works for Greenpeace. So Peter, welcome.
— Thanks a lot. It's good to be here.
— Now Peter, perhaps you could tell us something about Greenpeace and your job there?
— Sure. Well, I'll start by telling you roughly what Greenpeace is all about. I actually work in London for the Greenpeace organization. We've been going for a few decades and we're a nonviolent, nonpolitical organization.
zh: ——今早我们访谈环节的演播室里请到了彼得·威尔逊，他在绿色和平组织工作。彼得，欢迎。——谢谢，很高兴来到这儿。——彼得，能先给我们讲讲绿色和平和你在那儿的工作吗？——当然。我先大致说说绿色和平是做什么的。我其实在伦敦为该组织工作，我们成立已有几十年，是一个非暴力、非政治性的组织。

en:
We're involved in anti-nuclear activity, conservation and protection of animals, and protection and support of our ecosystem. I'm the action organizer and arrange any protests.
— A pretty important role. Peter, what sort of protests would you organize?
— Well, recently we've been involved in anti-nuclear campaigns. I personally arranged for the demonstration against radioactive waste dumping in the Atlantic Ocean. We've got a few small Greenpeace boats that we harass the dumping ships with.
— Hold on, Peter.
zh: 我们参与反核行动、动物保育与保护，以及生态系统的保护与支持。我是行动组织者，负责安排各种抗议。——这角色挺重要。彼得，你会组织什么样的抗议？——嗯，最近我们在做反核运动。我本人组织了反对向大西洋倾倒放射性废料的示威。我们有几艘绿色和平的小艇，用来干扰那些倾倒船。——等一下，彼得。

en:
— Tell me, Peter, what makes Harrods so famous?
— Well, it's the biggest department store in the UK, and its food hall and Egyptian hall are very famous. People come to Harrods just to see them.
— What is special about the food hall?
— It sells many different kinds of food. For example, it has 250 kinds of cheese from all over the world and more than 180 kinds of bread. Customers also love all the different kinds of chocolate.
zh: ——彼得，给我讲讲，哈罗德百货为什么这么有名？——嗯，它是英国最大的百货公司，食品厅和埃及厅尤其出名，很多人专程来哈罗德看这两处。——食品厅有什么特别？——它卖很多种食品，比如来自世界各地250种奶酪、180多种面包，顾客也特别喜欢各式各样的巧克力。

en:
We use 11,500 light bulbs.
— Really. Tell me, how many customers do you have on an average day, and how much do they spend?
— About 30,000 people come on an average day. But during the sales, the number increases to 300,000 customers a day.
— How much do they spend?
— Well, on average, customers spend about 1. 5 million pounds a day. The record for one day is 9 million pounds.
— 9 million pounds in one day?
zh: 我们用了11500只灯泡。——真的？那平均每天有多少顾客、消费多少？——平时一天大约3万人，打折季会涨到一天30万人次。——他们花多少钱？——嗯，平均每天顾客消费约150万英镑，单日纪录是900万英镑。——一天900万英镑？

en:
— Hello and welcome to our program Working Abroad. Our guest this evening is a Londoner who lives and works in Italy. Her name's Susan Hill. Susan, welcome to the program. You live in Florence — how long have you been living there?
— Since 1982. But when I went there in 1982, I planned to stay for only six months.
— Why did you change your mind?
— Well, I'm a designer. I design leather goods, mainly shoes and handbags.
zh: ——大家好，欢迎收看《海外工作》节目。今晚的嘉宾是一位在意大利生活工作的伦敦人，苏珊·希尔。苏珊，欢迎。你住在佛罗伦萨，在那儿住多久了？——从1982年起。不过1982年去的时候，我本来只打算待六个月。——为什么改主意了？——嗯，我是设计师，主要设计皮革制品，鞋和手袋为主。

en:
And in the last four years I've also been designing for the British company Burberrys.
— What have you been designing for them?
— Mostly handbags and small leather goods.
— Has the fashion industry in Italy changed since 1982?
— Oh, yes. It's become a lot more competitive, because the quality of products from other countries has improved a lot. But Italian quality and design is still world famous.
— And do you ever think of returning to live in England?
— No, not really.
zh: 过去四年我也一直在为英国公司博柏利做设计。——你给他们设计什么？——主要是手袋和小件皮具。——1982年以来意大利的时尚产业有变化吗？——哦，变化很大，竞争激烈多了，因为其他国家产品的质量提升了不少。不过意大利的品质和设计依旧世界闻名。——有没有想过回英国住？——没怎么想过。

en:
— Hi Anne, welcome back. How was your trip to the States?
— Very busy. I had a lot of meetings, so of course I didn't have much time to see New York.
— What a pity. Actually, I have a trip there myself next week. Do you take my advice — do the "Well-being in the Air" program? It really works.
— Oh, I read about that in a magazine. You say it works?
— Yes.
zh: ——嗨，安妮，欢迎回来，美国之行怎么样？——忙得很，会特别多，当然也就没什么时间逛纽约了。——真可惜。其实我下周也要去。听我一句，试试"空中健康"计划，真的很管用。——哦，我在杂志上读到过，你说确实有效？——是的。

en:
I drank a lot of water and fruit juice, and I ate the meals on the well-being menu. They're lighter — they have fish, vegetables and noodles, for example. And I did some of the exercises in the program.
— Exercises on a plane?
— Yes. I didn't do many, of course — there isn't much space on a plane.
— How many passengers did the exercises?
— Not many.
— And how much champagne did they drink?
— A lot. It was more popular than mineral water.
zh: 我喝了很多水和果汁，也吃了健康菜单上的餐食，那些更清淡，比如有鱼、蔬菜和面条；我还做了计划里的一些动作。——在飞机上做运动？——对，当然做得不多，飞机上空间有限。——有多少乘客做了操？——不多。——那他们喝了多少香槟？——很多，香槟比矿泉水受欢迎多了。

en: From California to Connecticut, babies sit on the laps of their parents or caretakers and are spoken to in Italian, French, Spanish and, increasingly, Chinese. They sit in circles, distracted by cuddly toys, at schools such as the Language Workshop in New York, or in formal groups organized by parents. There have been several studies that have found advantages in starting children off in a new language at a young age.
zh: 从加利福尼亚到康涅狄格，宝宝们坐在父母或看护人腿上，被用意大利语、法语、西班牙语，以及越来越多的中文跟他们说话。在纽约"语言工作坊"这样的学校里，或家长组织的小组里，他们围坐成一圈，被毛绒玩具分着心。已有多项研究发现，让孩子从小接触一门新语言是有好处的。

en: It is not necessary in our class. For clarity, we have to repeat the word until the idea sinks in. Some parents fear that with all these different words and languages, their children will have a harder time picking up English or will get confused. But scientists have found no such disadvantage to being multilingual.
zh: 在我们班上没有这个必要。为了讲清楚，我们得反复重复这个词，直到概念印进脑子里。有些家长担心，接触这么多不同的词和语言，孩子学英语会更吃力，或者会混淆。但科学家并未发现多语会带来这类不利影响。

en: There are emerging theories that the brain is designed to pick up multiple languages early in life, and that our current monolingual focus is actually a setback of evolution. Some research shows there is a window in which children can most readily absorb new languages: for the first six months of life, for example, babies can hear every sound from every language in the world.
zh: 一些新出现的理论认为，大脑天生就是为了在生命早期吸收多种语言，而我们当下只重单一语言的做法，其实是进化上的一种倒退。有研究显示，儿童最易吸收新语言存在一个窗口期：例如出生后的头六个月里，婴儿能听辨世界上所有语言里的所有音。

en: He was influenced by a group of artists called the Surrealists, who combined images in unusual and often strange ways. Joseph Cornell started making his own works by cutting out different pictures and putting them together in creative and magical combinations. Soon he started making boxes, inside of which were carefully arranged pictures and objects. He worked on his art at night after finishing his day job.
zh: 他受到一群被称为超现实主义者的影响，这些人以不寻常、常常古怪的方式把图像组合在一起。约瑟夫·康奈尔开始创作自己的作品：剪下各种图片，再以富有创意、如魔法般的组合拼贴起来。很快他开始做盒子，在盒内精心摆放图片和物件。他白天上完班，晚上做艺术。

en: Later, when his boxes and images started selling and receiving public recognition, he worked on his art full time. Joseph Cornell died in 1972. The Smithsonian exhibit showed almost 200 works made during his 40-year career. One work is called "Soap Bubble Set": a box with a glass window shows a map of the moon, several pictures of sea creatures, two glass cups and two white pipes for smoking.
zh: 后来，当他的盒子和图像开始卖出去、获得公众认可，他便全职投入创作。康奈尔1972年去世。史密森尼的展览展出了他40年生涯中近200件作品。其中一件叫《肥皂泡套装》：一只带玻璃窗的盒子里，呈现着一幅月球图、几张海洋生物图片、两只玻璃杯和两只白色烟斗。

en: A sophomore at Colorado State University first had a problem in taking tests when she began college. She said that she was well prepared for her tests. Sometimes she studied for weeks before a test, yet she would go in to take the test only to find she could not answer the questions correctly. She would blank out because of nervousness and fear. She couldn't think of the answer. Her low grades made her teachers surprised.
zh: 科罗拉多州立大学一名大二学生刚入学时第一次遇到考试问题。她说自己备考很充分，有时考前会复习好几周，可一进考场却发现答不对题。她会因紧张和恐惧而大脑一片空白，想不起答案。她的低分让老师们很惊讶。

en: Recently, test anxiety has been recognized as a real problem, not just an excuse or a false explanation of lazy students. There are some special counseling courses in universities trying to help students with the same problem. In these courses, counselors try to help students by teaching them how to manage test anxiety. At some universities, students are asked to take tests to measure their anxiety.
zh: 近来，考试焦虑已被承认是一个真实存在的问题，而不只是懒学生找的借口或假托之词。一些大学开设了专门的辅导课程来帮助有同样困扰的学生，咨询师通过教他们管理考试焦虑来提供帮助。有些学校还会让学生做测试来测量焦虑水平。

en: If the tests show that their anxiety level is high, the students will take short courses to help them deal with their tension. These courses teach students how to relax their bodies. Students are trained to become calm in very tense situations. By controlling their nervousness, they can let their minds work easily, and their learned information then comes out without difficulty on a test.
zh: 如果测试显示焦虑水平偏高，学生就要上短期课程学习应对紧张。这些课程教他们如何放松身体，训练他们在高度紧张的情境下保持平静。控制住紧张之后，思维就能顺畅运转，学到的知识在考场上也就自然地呼之欲出了。

en: Perlman supports the findings of the study and adds that it is a sounder idea to keep children with other children, as in a daycare center, than it is to have children cared for by a babysitter. According to the results of the study, infants benefit from being in the company of other babies on a daily basis.
zh: 珀尔曼支持这项研究的结论，并补充说，把孩子和其他孩子放在一起（比如托儿所）比请保姆单独照看更妥当。按研究结果，婴儿每天有别的宝宝作伴是有益处的。

en: The American patent system, provided for in the Constitution, was designed to encourage the creation and use of new technology. An inventor would describe an invention both in writing and with drawings, and submit the description with a model to a government official. This was a big improvement from the past, when patents were submitted directly to the Secretary of State. Now, if the invention was judged to be new and useful, the official would give the inventor a patent.
zh: 宪法中规定设立的美国专利制度，旨在鼓励新技术的创造与应用。发明人要既有文字说明又有图纸，并把说明连同模型一并提交给政府官员。相比过去直接把专利交给国务卿，这是一大进步。如今，若一项发明被判定新颖且有用，官员就会授予发明人专利。

en: The patent meant that for 14 years — later changed to 17 years — the inventor owned the new invention. Inventors could license their ideas to manufacturers or just use them themselves. The government would not issue any other patent for the same idea, and the inventor could sue anyone who used the patented idea without paying the owner of the patent for permission to use it. A useful patent meant that the inventor could make a lot of money.
zh: 专利意味着在14年（后改为17年）内，发明人拥有这项新发明。发明人可以把点子授权给厂商，也可以自己使用；政府不会再就同一构想颁发别的专利，而且对于未经专利权人许可、未付费就使用该专利的人，发明人有权起诉。一项有用的专利能让发明人赚很多钱。

en: From 1912 to 1915 he lived in New England, where he became friendly with several poets, including Edward Thomas, and published A Boy's Will in 1913 and North of Boston in 1914. In America, his poetry was soon admired, and he was awarded the Pulitzer Prize on four occasions between 1924 and 1943. He went on writing throughout his life, publishing Steeple Bush at the age of 72. He died in 1963.
zh: 1912至1915年间，他住在新英格兰，与包括爱德华·托马斯在内的几位诗人交好，并于1913年出版《少年的意志》、1914年出版《波士顿以北》。在美国，他的诗很快受到推崇，1924到1943年间四次获普利策奖。他一生笔耕不辍，72岁时还出版了《尖塔灌木》。1963年去世。

en: Frost's poems are revolutionary because they lack the exaggeration of rhetoric. Many of his lines and sentences are plain, and in themselves nothing, but they are bound together and made beautiful by a calm eagerness of emotion. With his close, observant eye and touch, we can feel the daily activities of farming and the landscape that is their background.
zh: 弗罗斯特的诗之所以具有革新性，是因为它去掉了修辞上的夸张。他的许多诗行和句子都很朴素，单看本身平平无奇，却被一种平静而热切的情感串在一起、变得动人。凭着他细致入微的观察眼光与笔触，我们能感受到农事的日常，以及作为其背景的乡野景色。

en: The average person learns most of the 30,000 to 40,000 words whose meanings we recognize by hearing them or getting familiar with them in context without conscious effort. The best way to build a good vocabulary, therefore, is to read a great deal and to participate in a lot of good conversations. There are relatively few words that we learn permanently by purposefully referring to dictionaries or keeping word lists. Here are some suggestions on how to do it.
zh: 我们能认出词义的三四万个词，大多是在无意识中通过听到它们、或在语境里熟悉它们而学会的。因此，扩充词汇量最好的办法就是大量阅读、多参与有质量的交谈。靠特意查词典、列单词表而永久记住的词其实相对很少。下面给出几条具体建议。

en: If you are really conscientious, write the word and its meaning in a personal vocabulary list. Go over the list from time to time. Further, try to use the new word in writing or conversation a few times over the next several days. Listen to good conversations and be alert to new words you hear or to new meanings of words you have already known. Then treat them just as you treat the new words you read.
zh: 如果你真的很用心，就把单词和释义写进自己的词汇本，时不时翻一翻。接下来几天里，再试着在写作或谈话中用上几次这个新词。多听有质量的交谈，留意听到的新词，或已认识的词出现的新义，然后像处理阅读中遇到的生词那样对待它们。

en: Telephone books in the United States have white, blue and yellow pages. The white pages list people with phones by last name. The blue pages contain numbers of city services, government agencies and public schools. Businesses and professional services are listed in a special section, the yellow pages. To make a long distance call, you need an area code. Each area in the US has an area code. The area covered by one area code may be small or large.
zh: 美国的电话簿有白页、蓝页和黄页。白页按姓氏列出装电话的个人；蓝页收录市政服务、政府机构和公立学校的号码；工商与专业服务则列在专门的黄页里。打长途电话需要区号，美国每个地区都有一个区号，一个区号覆盖的范围可大可小。

en: If you are making a long distance call on a public phone and run out of money, give the number on your phone to the person you're talking to, then hang up the receiver and he can call you back. If you make a long distance call and get a wrong number, call the operator and explain what happened. This means that you can make the call again to the right number without having to pay more money.
zh: 如果你用公用电话打长途时钱用完了，就把你这部电话的号码告诉对方，然后挂断，让他回拨给你。如果打长途拨错了号码，就打给接线员说明情况，这样你可以免费重拨正确号码，不必再付一次钱。

en: We know that we have to pay for what we get. If we buy food, we know there will be a bill to pay. These are private bills. But there are also public bills that must be paid. Public bills are paid for by the government. In turn, we get these services through taxes. What would happen if everyone in the city stopped paying taxes? The water supply would stop. Water might even become unclean and impure.
zh: 我们知道，得到什么就得付钱。买食物，我们知道会有账单要付，这些是私人账单；但也有必须支付的公共账单，由政府来付，而我们则通过税收获得这些服务。假如城里所有人都不交税会怎样？供水会停，水甚至可能变得不干净、不纯净。

en: More than three quarters of the money spent by our government is used for this purpose. The next large amount of public money goes to teach and train our citizens. Billions of dollars each year are spent on schools and libraries. Public money is used to pay the teachers and all the public officials. Also, a large amount of public funds is spent on roads. The greatest part of the needed funds is raised by taxes.
zh: 政府支出中有四分之三以上用在这个用途上；第二大部分公共资金用于教育和培训公民，每年有数十亿美元花在学校和图书馆上。公共资金用来支付教师和所有公职人员的薪酬，还有很大一部分花在道路上。所需资金的最大部分靠税收筹集。

en: For example, National Savings Bank offers work on a half-time basis — that's 20 hours a week. Retail stores and restaurants have positions requiring fewer hours. Even less time is expected of those providing childcare. We have a number of families registered with us who are looking for babysitters for as few as four hours a week. For students who prefer outdoor work, there are seasonal positions right on campus, working with the gardening and landscaping teams.
zh: 比如国民储蓄银行提供半职岗位，也就是每周20小时；零售店和餐馆有工时更少的职位；做托儿工作的岗位所需时间更少。我们登记了不少家庭，找每周只做四小时的保姆。对于更喜欢户外工作的学生，校园里就有季节性岗位，跟园艺和绿化团队一起干活。

en: These often require the most time, and they are the least flexible in terms of scheduling. To see a complete list of these and other available jobs — including the salary offered and the hours required — stop by our office and be sure to bring a resume with you. When you find something that interests you, we'll put you in touch with the person offering it. In addition, our counselors will give you hints about successful interviewing.
zh: 这类岗位往往最耗时间，排班上也最不灵活。想看这类及其他在招岗位的完整清单——包括提供的薪资和所需工时——欢迎来我们办公室，记得带上简历。看到感兴趣的岗位，我们会把你和招聘方对接上。此外，我们的顾问还会给你一些面试成功的窍门。

en: The main reason for the widespread demand for English is its present importance as a world language. Besides serving the indefinite needs of its native speakers, English is a language in which some of the important works in science, technology and other fields are being produced — and not always by native speakers. It is widely used for such purposes as airport communications, international conferences, and the spread of information over the radio and television networks of many nations.
zh: 英语需求如此广泛，主因在于它作为世界语言当下的地位。除了满足母语者难以计数的需要，科学、技术等领域部分重要著作也是用英语写成的——而且作者未必是母语者。它被广泛用于机场通信、国际会议，以及许多国家广播电视网络的信息传播。

en: The podcast revolution is erupting all over the world, and seemingly all at once. Why is it getting so popular? The technology is simple to master and podcasting software is inexpensive — sometimes even free. Two Chinese students are receiving international fame as millions of people around the world watch them podcast from their dormitory. They are called the "Back Dormitory Boys," and they specialize in miming Backstreet Boys songs.
zh: 播客革命正在世界各地、而且几乎同时爆发。它为什么这么火？技术容易掌握，播客软件又便宜，有时甚至免费。两名中国学生因为在宿舍里做播客被全球数百万人观看而声名远扬，人称"后舍男生"，专攻对口型表演后街男孩的歌曲。

en: Although most people in China don't have iPods, podcasting is sweeping the country. The Back Dormitory Boys are among the thousands of Chinese who are putting their own homemade audio and video up on the internet for all to enjoy. "You just gotta love two guys making a fool of themselves and gaining international attention," says Good Morning America technology expert Becky Worley. The internet is becoming more and more popular with China's youth.
zh: 尽管多数中国人没有 iPod，播客仍席卷全国。后舍男生只是成千上万把自己制作的音频视频传到网上供人欣赏的中国人之一。《早安美国》科技专家贝琪·沃利说："两个小伙子出洋相还赢得国际关注，你就是忍不住喜欢。"互联网在中国年轻人中越来越普及。

en: Banks and stock markets will be closed on Saturdays. Staff of the civil service will be forced out of their offices two Saturdays a month. The government hopes that others will follow that practice. But some persuasion will be needed. Small companies are very angry about it and they fear competitors may not cut hours. The unions are no happier. They have even advertised in newspapers arguing their case against the foreign pressure that is forcing leisure upon them.
zh: 银行和股市周六将休市，公务员每月两个周六将被"请"出办公室。政府希望其他行业照此办理，但还需要做些说服工作：小公司对此非常恼火，担心竞争对手不减工时；工会同样不高兴，甚至登报陈述反对理由，抱怨是外来压力把闲暇强加给他们。

en: They say that shorter hours are a disguised pay cut. The industrialists, who have no objection to the government's plans, admit that shorter hours will help them cut costs. Younger Japanese, who are supposed to be acting against their hard-working parents, show no sign of wanting time off either. But unlike older workers, they do spend money in their spare time.
zh: 他们说，缩短工时是变相减薪。对政府计划并无异议的实业家也承认，缩短工时有助于他们削减成本。本该与勤勉父辈唱反调的日本年轻人，同样没有想休假的迹象；只不过和年长员工不同，他们确实会在空闲时间花钱。

en: Many advertisers embraced a genuine concern for the environment, but consumers realized that some companies made false claims and exploited the movement, using such nebulous terms as "environmentally friendly" and "green. " Consumers grew wary of environmental appeals, and advertisers reacted by reducing its emphasis. Two legal guidelines paved the road to a second wave. In 1992, the Federal Trade Commission established guidelines for green marketing, followed shortly by state governments.
zh: 许多广告主真心关注环保，但消费者发现有些公司做虚假宣称、利用这场运动，用"环保""绿色"这类含糊字眼。消费者对环保诉求变得警惕，广告主于是降低了这方面的强调。两项法规为第二波浪潮铺了路：1992年联邦贸易委员会出台绿色营销指南，各州政府随后跟进。

en: In America, driver's education is part of the regular high school curriculum. Every student in his or her second year of high school is required to take a class in driver's education. However, unlike other courses, it is not given during the regular school year; instead it is a summer course. The course is divided into two parts: class time for learning laws and regulations, and driving time to practice. Driving class time is not unlike any other class.
zh: 在美国，驾驶培训是高中常规课程的一部分，每名高二学生都必须修一门驾驶教育课。不过与其他课程不同，它不在正常学年开设，而是暑期课程。课程分两部分：课堂学习法规，以及实际上车练习。课堂部分和别的课没什么两样。

en: The students have a text from which they study the basic laws they must know. Driving time is a chance for the students to practice starting, steering, backing up, parking, switching lanes, turning corners and all the other maneuvers required. Each student is required to drive a total of six hours. The students are divided into groups of four. The students and the instructor go out driving for two hours.
zh: 学生有一本教材，用来学习必须掌握的基本法规；上车练习则让他们实践起步、转向、倒车、停车、变道、转弯，以及其他所有必需的操作。每名学生须累计驾驶六小时，四人一组，学生和教练一起外出驾驶两小时。

en: The pioneer of chocolate cookies in America is Amos Cookies. Amos was a talent agent at the William Morris Agency who used home-baked chocolate chip cookies as a calling card. After a while, some of his famous clients began encouraging him to sell the cookies. They even invested in the Famous Amos Cookie Company, which he started in 1975, making him one of the pioneers of the gourmet cookie trend. Sales at Famous Amos hit 12 million dollars by 1982.
zh: 美国巧克力曲奇的先驱是"阿莫斯曲奇"。阿莫斯原是威廉·莫里斯经纪公司的艺人经纪，把家里烤的巧克力豆曲奇当名片用。过了一阵，他那些名人客户开始劝他把曲奇拿去卖，甚至为他1975年创办的"著名阿莫斯曲奇公司"投资，让他成为精品曲奇风潮的开创者之一。到1982年，公司销售额已达1200万美元。

en: His cookies were a success, but he was no manager, and his company started losing money. Amos had to bring in new money. From 1985 to 1988, he went through four different co-owners. Each time a change was made, Amos gave up more of his share of the pie. By the time the Shanby Group bought it in 1988, Amos had nothing left. He even signed away his trademark "Amos.
zh: 他的曲奇很成功，可他并不擅长经营，公司开始亏损，阿莫斯不得不引入新资金。1985到1988年间，他先后换过四位共同所有人；每次变动，他让出的份额都更多一些。等到1988年尚比集团收购时，阿莫斯已一无所有，甚至连"Amos"这个商标也签字让了出去。

en: There is no doubt that adults, and even highly educated adults, vary greatly in the speed and efficiency of their reading. Some proceed very slowly throughout; others dash along too quickly and then have to go back again. Poor readers in particular may lack the ability to vary their manner of reading according to the type of reading matter and their intentions in reading it.
zh: 毫无疑问，成年人、哪怕是受过高等教育的成年人，阅读速度和效率也差别很大。有人从头到尾读得很慢，有人一路猛冲太快、又得回头重读。尤其阅读能力差的人，可能不会根据读物类型和阅读目的去调整自己的读法。

en: Therefore, even light reading matter gives him little pleasure, because he reads so slowly. But this pace may be too fast for really difficult material, which requires special concentration at difficult points. A type of reading which needs careful attention to detail is proofreading. In order to detect misprints in a sample print, the reader needn't notice so much the meaning of what he reads as the exact shape and order of words in the text.
zh: 因此，连轻松的读物也给不了他多少乐趣，因为他读得太慢；可这个速度对真正难的材料又可能太快，后者需要在难点上特别专注。校样校对就是一种需要细究细节的阅读：要从一份印样里找出错字，读者不必太在意所读内容的意思，倒更该留意文字的确切形状与顺序。

en: Twenty-five years ago, Ray Anderson, a single parent with a one-year-old son, was returning home on Christmas Eve when he witnessed a horrible accident. The driver of a truck ran a red light and hit the car of Sandra Jenkins. That killed Sandra instantly, but her three-month-old daughter was trapped upside down in the burning wreckage.
zh: 25年前，带着一岁儿子的单亲父亲雷·安德森在平安夜回家途中目睹了一场惨烈事故：一辆卡车司机闯红灯，撞上桑德拉·詹金斯的汽车。桑德拉当场身亡，而她三个月大的女儿被困在燃烧的残骸里，身子倒悬着。

en: Two hours later, Anderson died — but this heroic act was published widely in the media. Anderson's son was soon adopted by relatives, and the family moved to the East Coast. What really drew public attention were some other details beyond the accident. According to the newspaper, Anderson was on a mission of love that fateful Christmas Eve, in the process of distributing care packages to needy families in the area.
zh: 两小时后安德森也去世了，但这一义举被媒体广泛报道。他的儿子很快被亲戚收养，全家搬到了东海岸。真正引起公众注意的，是事故之外的另一些细节：据报纸说，那个命运攸关的平安夜，安德森正执行一项爱心任务——给当地贫困家庭分发慰问物资包。

en: A beetle invasion in the United States has killed at least 20 million ash trees. The invasion of the emerald ash borer was first discovered near Detroit, Michigan. Experts believe the small green insects arrived in the 1990s in shipments of goods from East Asia. The emerald ash borer has destroyed trees in the Midwest and as far east in the United States as Maryland. The insects have also spread as far north as Ontario, Canada.
zh: 美国一场甲虫入侵已害死至少2000万棵白蜡树。白蜡窄吉丁最早是在密歇根州底特律附近被发现的。专家认为，这种小小的绿色昆虫是上世纪90年代随东亚货物运抵的。它已毁掉中西部、乃至东至马里兰州的树木，还向北扩散到加拿大的安大略省。

en: Ash trees can resist many diseases, but they cannot resist the emerald ash borer. It lays eggs on the bark. The young larvae drill into and feed on the inner bark. This harms the ability of the tree to transport water and nutrition. In some places, farmers are using detection trees. They have an area where bark has been cut away. The area circles the tree. The process weakens the tree.
zh: 白蜡树能抵抗多种病害，却挡不住白蜡窄吉丁。它把卵产在树皮上，孵化出的幼虫钻进内皮取食，损害树木输送水分和养分的能力。有些地方，农民使用"诱捕树"：在树干上剥去一圈树皮，环绕整棵树，这种做法会削弱树势。

en: It examines and X-rays the seeds to make sure there are no living borer fertilized eggs; only the best seeds are retained and then sent for storage in a seed bank. There they are dried and frozen. Should the seeds ever be needed, the hope is that scientists might someday develop an ash tree that could resist the little green attackers.
zh: 它对种子做检查并做 X 光透视，确保没有存活的吉丁受精卵；只留下最好的种子，送去种子库保存，在那里进行干燥和冷冻。万一将来用得上，人们希望科学家终有一天能培育出抵抗这种绿色小侵略者的白蜡树。

en: Majestic. Serene. Just two words to describe the scenic regions of Utah in the mountain West of the United States. Now our office offers fabulous five-day outdoor packages to the state for the adventurous. On the first day of your tour, visit the capital of historic Salt Lake City — Temple Square, home to the world-famous Mormon Tabernacle Choir, and other local historical sites.
zh: 壮丽。宁静。两个词便足以形容美国西部山区的犹他州胜景。现在我们办公室为爱冒险的人推出精彩的五日户外套餐。行程第一天，造访历史名城、州府盐湖城——以世界闻名的摩门会幕合唱团所在地圣殿广场，以及其他当地历史遗迹。

en: You'll also hike and scramble up to remote Indian ruins, study their history along the way, and learn how to respect and preserve the sites and wildlife you encounter. You also learn the basics in rappelling techniques designed specifically for the amateur climber. The price of your package includes local transportation in Utah, one night's lodging in a four-star hotel in Salt Lake City, hiking and camping gear, two meals a day, and your professional tour guide.
zh: 你还会徒步攀爬，前往偏远的印第安遗址，沿途了解它们的历史，并学会尊重和保护所遇见的遗迹与野生动物；还会学到专为业余攀登者设计的基础绳降技巧。套餐价格包含犹他州当地交通、盐湖城四星级酒店一晚住宿、徒步与露营装备、每日两餐，以及专业导游。

en: America continues to lead the world as a destination for international students. Last year, about 900,000 foreign students were studying in the United States, about half of them from Asia. But a growing number of Asian students are looking to an English-speaking country much closer to home: the Philippines. The island nation of 100 million is quickly becoming the education center of Asia. The country's low prices, open culture and quality schools are attracting record numbers of foreign students.
zh: 美国仍是全球首屈一指的留学目的地。去年约90万名外国学生在美就读，其中约一半来自亚洲。但越来越多亚洲学生把目光投向离家更近的英语国家：菲律宾。这个拥有一亿人口的岛国正迅速成为亚洲的教育中心，低廉的价格、开放的文化和优质的学校吸引了创纪录数量的外国学生。

en: Today, the Philippines markets itself as the world's third-largest English-speaking country. The truth is, there are actually more people who speak English in the Philippines than the national language. English is learned even outside of school, because a lot of the communications are done in English — public signs are in English, television and internet are all in English. Low prices and its location in Asia helped to produce the education explosion in the Philippines.
zh: 如今菲律宾把自己宣传为世界第三大英语国家。实情是，说英语的菲律宾人其实比说本国语言的人还多。英语甚至不用在学校学，因为很多交流都用英语进行：公共标识是英文，电视和网络也都是英文。低物价加上地处亚洲，促成了菲律宾的教育爆炸。

en: Some Korean families even moved to the Philippines so that children can learn English in public schools. As in the US, schools in the Philippines range from world class to low-quality diploma mills. In most Asian countries, students learn English through grammar and translation from the mother language. In the Philippines, students are encouraged to practice speaking English in real-life situations. In general, there is less emphasis on grammar and error correction.
zh: 一些韩国家庭甚至举家搬到菲律宾，让孩子在公立学校学英语。和美国一样，菲律宾的学校也良莠不齐，从世界一流到劣质"文凭工厂"都有。多数亚洲国家靠语法和母语翻译来学英语，而菲律宾鼓励学生在真实情境中练口语，总体上对语法和纠错的强调更少。

en: It is digital only. The currency is created on computers by a community of people across the globe. Anyone can join that network or group, according to CoinDesk. com. This network processes transactions made with the digital currency. Bitcoins are stored in a digital wallet, over the internet or on the user's computer. There is not an unlimited amount of bitcoins. Nakamoto set up rules to limit the currency to 21 million bitcoins.
zh: 它完全是数字化的。据 CoinDesk 网站，这种货币由遍布全球的一群人在计算机上创造出来，任何人都能加入这个网络，由它处理用该数字货币进行的交易。比特币存放在数字钱包里，可以在网上，也可以在用户自己的电脑上。比特币并非无限量，中本聪设定了规则，把总量限制在2100万枚。

en: For example, bitcoins are being used by ISIS terrorists to fund operations, according to Ghost Security Group, a counterterrorism network that focuses on the internet and social media. Morgan Wright is a cybersecurity expert and senior fellow at the Center for Digital Government, a national research and advisory institute on information technology policies. "Terrorists need anonymity," Wright told Fox News. "Countries have gotten very good at tracking terror financing in the years since 9/11.
zh: 例如，据专注互联网与社交媒体的反恐网络"幽灵安全组织"称，"伊斯兰国"恐怖分子正用比特币为行动筹资。摩根·赖特是网络安全专家、数字政府中心高级研究员，该中心是研究信息技术政策的全国性咨询机构。"恐怖分子需要匿名，"赖特对福克斯新闻说，"9·11之后这些年，各国在追踪恐怖融资方面已经做得非常好了。"

en: 8 million Bitcoin wallets globally. According to Wired, you can also buy and sell bitcoins on BitQuick, Zapoo and CoinCorner, among other exchanges. It is possible to do complex financial trades with bitcoins, such as futures, options and swaps. The price of bitcoins on online exchanges has fluctuated widely, which has led to speculation in the digital currency. In 2009 and early 2010, bitcoins had no value at all, said Wired.
zh: 全球共有800万个比特币钱包。据《连线》杂志，你也可以在 BitQuick、Zapoo、CoinCorner 等交易所买卖比特币，还能用它做期货、期权、掉期等复杂金融交易。网上交易所的比特币价格波动剧烈，引来了对这种数字货币的投机。《连线》说，2009年和2010年初，比特币根本一文不值。

en: However, if it does not, there are various means the consumer may use to gain satisfaction. A simple and common method used by many consumers is to complain directly to the store manager. In general, the higher up his or her complaint, the faster he or she can expect it to be settled. In such a case, it is usually settled in the consumer's favor, assuming he or she has a just claim.
zh: 但如果商家没有这样做，消费者还有多种办法讨回公道。许多人用的一个简单常见办法，是直接向门店经理投诉。一般来说，投诉层级越高，问题解决得越快；只要诉求合理，这类投诉通常会以对消费者有利的方式了结。

en: If this cannot be done, the consumer will succeed best by presenting specific information as to what is wrong rather than by making general statements. For example, "the left speaker does not work at all and the sound coming out of the right one is unclear" is better than "this stereo does not work. The store manager may advise the consumer to write to the manufacturer.
zh: 如果做不到这一点，消费者最好具体说明哪里出了问题，而不是笼统地讲。比如"左音箱完全不响，右声道出来的声音也不清楚"就胜过"这套音响坏了"。门店经理可能会建议消费者写信给厂商。

en: Today we have good news for all our coffee drinkers around the world. A new study finds that drinking coffee can help you live longer. Researchers at the Harvard School of Public Health recently discovered that drinking between three and five cups of coffee a day may prevent certain illnesses. They found that coffee can protect against heart disease, brain diseases and suicide. Walter Willett is a nutrition researcher at Harvard and co-author of the study.
zh: 今天给全世界爱喝咖啡的人带来一个好消息：一项新研究发现，喝咖啡可能有助于延寿。哈佛公共卫生学院的研究人员最近发现，每天喝三到五杯咖啡或可预防某些疾病——咖啡能防范心脏病、脑部疾病和自杀。沃尔特·威利特是哈佛的营养学研究员，也是该研究的合著者。

en: We found that moderate coffee drinking was linked with a reduced risk of death from many diseases. However, we found no link between coffee drinking and cancer. We also considered other habits such as smoking, obesity and how active the subjects were. We also looked at what kinds of food the subjects ate, as well as how much alcohol and what type of alcohol they drank. "Our research adds to a growing body of evidence.
zh: 我们发现，适量喝咖啡与多种疾病的死亡风险降低相关；但没有发现喝咖啡与癌症之间有联系。我们还考虑了吸烟、肥胖、受试者的活动量等其他习惯，也考察了受试者吃什么样的食物、喝多少酒、喝哪类酒。"我们的研究为越来越多的证据再添一笔。"

en: Hu adds the data from the study support that drinking a moderate amount of coffee can be part of a healthy diet, but how much and when you drink coffee is important. Nevertheless, our study also received doubts and criticism. Andrew Maynard of Arizona State University claims that the health benefits documented in this new study are small.
zh: 胡补充说，研究数据支持"适量喝咖啡可以是健康饮食的一部分"，但喝多少、什么时候喝很重要。不过我们的研究也收到了质疑和批评：亚利桑那州立大学的安德鲁·梅纳德就认为，这项新研究记录到的健康收益其实很小。

en: These are the exact words of Mahesh Thakar. He is head of research in the Department of Neurology at the University of Missouri's School of Medicine. Thakar explains that when a person drinks alcohol, they get sleepy. He says a drug in cigarettes fights that sleepy feeling. That drug, nicotine, can be addictive. Smokers need more cigarettes because of their body's growing dependence on the drug.
zh: 这正是马赫什·塔卡尔的原话。他是密苏里大学医学院神经病学系的研究负责人。塔卡尔解释说，人喝酒后会犯困，而香烟里的一种药物会对抗这种困意——那就是尼古丁，它会让人上瘾。由于身体对它的依赖日益加深，吸烟者需要抽更多烟。

en: However, the new study shows a dependent relationship between the substances. Thakar says his team found that nicotine weakens the sleep-causing effects of alcohol. It does this by activating an area of the brain called the basal forebrain. According to the Psychology Definition website, that area is responsible for memory, learning and attention. For this new experiment, Thakar and his team used equipment that measures brain activity in rats.
zh: 然而新研究显示，这两种物质之间存在依赖关系。塔卡尔说，团队发现尼古丁会削弱酒精的催眠作用，其方式是激活大脑里一个叫"基底前脑"的区域。据心理学定义网站介绍，该区域负责记忆、学习和注意力。这次实验里，塔卡尔团队使用了测量大鼠脑活动的设备。

en: Until recently, blind and visually impaired students in Kenya were still using Braille books for their studies. But Kenyan schools for the blind are now beginning to adopt technology that provides material in an audible form — and in the process expands their opportunities. Lucas Munzia intently searches the internet for information. Today's class is on biology. Munzia is visually impaired and for the last two years has been attending computer classes at the Thika School for the Blind.
zh: 直到不久前，肯尼亚的盲人和视障学生还在用盲文课本学习。但如今肯尼亚的盲人学校开始采用能以声音提供材料的技术，并借此拓展他们的机会。卢卡斯·蒙齐亚正专注地在网上检索资料，今天这节课讲生物。蒙齐亚有视力障碍，过去两年一直在锡卡盲人学校上电脑课。

en: The school embraced assistive technology six years ago, enabling blind and visually impaired students to access information from computers and iPads. Zachary Muiza, one of the school's teachers, was born blind. He has been teaching the students how to use the technology for about two years now. He says the technology presents opportunities that can level the playing field for his students. "Assistive technology equips the learners with very many skills that really make them independent in life," he said.
zh: 这所学校六年前引入辅助技术，让盲人和视障学生能从电脑和 iPad 获取信息。该校教师扎卡里·穆伊扎生来失明，教学生使用这项技术已有约两年。他说，这项技术带来的机会能让学生站上更公平的起跑线："辅助技术让学习者掌握许多技能，真正使他们在生活中自立。"

en: "When learners move from primary to high school and then to universities, they go to university and then they realize there is not that technology. So the fact is that they learned that technology in primary and high school. When they move to university, they go back to Braille, which is another challenge to them. So far, four out of Kenya's 11 schools for the blind have adopted the technology.
zh: "学生从小学升到中学、再升到大学，进了大学才发现那里没有这套技术。事实是，他们在小学和中学学过这套技术，可一进大学又得回到盲文，这对他们是另一重挑战。"目前肯尼亚11所盲人学校中已有4所采用了该技术。

en: But does a person's body and face reveal the truth? Actually, using body language and facial expressions to catch someone in a lie is really hard. And it only works seemingly by chance. According to a new study carried out by researchers in the United Kingdom, talking is the best way to smoke out a liar. The study found that certain conversation-based techniques can help you recognize when a person is lying to you.
zh: 可一个人的身体和脸真能露出真相吗？实际上，靠肢体语言和表情识破谎言非常难，奏效看上去不过是碰运气。英国研究人员的一项新研究发现，交谈才是"熏出"说谎者的最好办法：某些基于对话的技巧，能帮你察觉对方正在撒谎。

en: Others depended instead on the person's body language, like lack of eye contact and showing signs of nervousness. The agents talking with the passengers were 20 times more likely to catch the liars. Here are some tips for catching a liar by using the conversational CCE method. One, use open-ended questions. These are the opposite of yes-and-no questions. Open-ended questions force the person to stretch the story of their lies until they get caught in their own web of lies.
zh: 另一些人则依赖对方的肢体语言，比如回避眼神接触、显出紧张迹象。而和乘客交谈的那些探员，识破说谎者的概率高出20倍。下面是用"对话式 CCE 方法"识谎的几条建议：第一，用开放式问题，也就是与"是/否"问题相反的那种。开放式问题会逼对方把谎话越编越长，最终陷在自己织的谎网里。

en: Hello, I'm Steve Ember. Today we tell about a man known as Johnny Appleseed. His real name was John Chapman. Little is known about John Chapman's childhood. When he was old enough to leave home, he slowly traveled south and west from Massachusetts to the state of Pennsylvania. He is said to have cleared land and planted apple seeds near a waterway. In a short time, the seeds grew to become trees that produced fruit.
zh: 大家好，我是史蒂夫·恩伯。今天讲一个人称"苹果佬约翰尼"的人，本名约翰·查普曼。关于他的童年几乎无人知晓。到了能离家的年纪，他从马萨诸塞州慢慢向南、向西走到宾夕法尼亚州。据说他曾在一条水道附近清出土地、种下苹果籽，没多久种子就长成结果的树。

en: Sometimes he gave away trees to needy settlers. When low on seeds, he returned east to Pennsylvania to get more. He got the seeds from apple presses — machines used to make apples into a drink called apple cider. Before long, Chapman's trees were growing in fields across Ohio. People began calling him Johnny Appleseed. Johnny Appleseed was a small man with lots of energy. He had long, dark hair; his eyes were black and bright. He never married.
zh: 有时他把树苗送给贫困的拓荒者；种子快用完时，就回东边的宾夕法尼亚再取。种子来自苹果压榨机——把苹果做成苹果酒的机器。不久，查普曼的树就长遍俄亥俄州的田野，人们开始叫他"苹果佬约翰尼"。他个子不高却精力充沛，深色长发，眼睛又黑又亮，一生未婚。

en: Bad news for the delivery guys: you might have to start thinking about finding a new job very soon, because delivery men bringing items to home may become a thing of the past one day. Well, I may have exaggerated the situation a little bit, but what I'm going to tell you next is dead true.
zh: 给送货小哥们一个坏消息：你也许很快就得考虑另找工作了，因为把东西送到家门口的配送员，说不定哪天就成了历史。好吧，我可能把情况说得夸张了一点，但接下来要告诉你的是千真万确的。

en: Lightweight, it can only carry a small amount in its top compartment: two grocery bags, or small packages up to nine kilograms. The company's chief executive officer, who also co-founded Skype, said the unnamed robot is practical, safe and environmentally friendly. A user would place an order online as people do right now, but instead of getting the delivery by somebody coming up to and knocking on your door, you would get it by a robot.
zh: 它很轻，顶部货舱只能装少量东西：两袋食品杂货，或最多九公斤的小包裹。该公司首席执行官也是 Skype 的联合创始人，他说这台尚未命名的机器人实用、安全、环保。用户照现在这样在线下单，但不再是有人上门敲门送货，而是由机器人送到。

en: We call up the delivery using our smartphone, and then the robot gets loaded with our parcel and drives to our doorstep. Once the robot gets moving, using a navigation system that also helps it avoid pedestrians, the customer can use the smartphone app to track it and, upon arrival, unlock the compartment. You must be thinking about thieves, aren't you? Actually, a lot of thought has been put into protecting the robot from thievery.
zh: 我们用智能手机呼叫配送，机器人装上包裹后开到家门口。一旦启动，它靠导航系统行进，还能借此避让行人；顾客可用手机应用追踪它，到达时解锁货舱。你肯定在想小偷吧？其实，为防偷盗已经费了不少心思。

en: Welcome to Leadership Insider. It is an online course that invites the most thoughtful and influential people in business to contribute answers to questions about careers and leadership. Let me introduce to you Sanjay Sango, the COO of Delos Capital, who will answer the question: how do you stay humble at work? In today's business environment, confidence is a key attribute for success.
zh: 欢迎来到《领导力内幕》。这是一门在线课程，邀请商界最有思想、最有影响力的人来回答关于职业与领导力的问题。让我介绍德洛斯资本首席运营官桑杰·桑戈，他将回答这个问题：如何在工作中保持谦逊？在当今商业环境里，自信是成功的关键特质。

en: This worked for a while, but then my unwarranted confidence led to setbacks in the form of careless mistakes and lack of attention to details, which was noticed by my superiors as well as clients. While it is tough to realize that I was not the financial genius I imagined myself to be, it also taught me to be humble and recognize that I had a lot more work to do to become proficient in my field.
zh: 这么做管用过一阵，可后来我那份毫无根据的自信带来了挫折：粗心的失误、对细节的疏忽，上级和客户都看在眼里。虽然承认自己并非想象中的金融天才是件难受的事，但它也教会我谦逊，让我明白要在本行做到熟练，还有很长的路要走。

en: If you really want to impress your superiors — or if you are a leader and want to impress your team — do your homework first. A bad decision made in the heat of eagerness will hurt your credibility in the long run. Second, ask plenty of questions. Obviously, not every question goes to your boss's desk, and sometimes it's better to ask your peers or even your juniors first.
zh: 如果你真想让上级刮目相看——或者你是领导者、想让团队信服——先把功课做足。一时头脑发热做出的糟糕决定，长远看会损害你的可信度。第二，多提问。当然，不是每个问题都要端到老板桌上，有时先问同事、甚至先问下属反而更好。

en: Hi, I'm Elizabeth Hoffler, Master of Social Work. I am a social worker, a lobbyist and a special assistant to the executive director at the National Association of Social Workers. Today we're going to be talking about becoming a social worker. Social work is the helping profession. Its primary mission is to enhance human well-being and help meet the basic needs of all people, with a particular focus on those who are vulnerable, oppressed and living in poverty.
zh: 嗨，我是社会工作硕士伊丽莎白·霍夫勒，一名社会工作者、游说者，也是全国社会工作者协会执行主任的特别助理。今天我们来聊聊如何成为一名社会工作者。社会工作是助人的专业，首要使命是增进人的福祉、帮助满足所有人的基本需要，尤其关注脆弱者、受压迫者和生活贫困的人。

en: People from every age, every background, across the country — wherever needed, social workers come to help. The most well-known aspect of the profession is that of a social safety net. We help guide people to critical resources and counsel them on life-changing decisions. There are more than 600,000 professional social workers in the country, and we all either have a bachelor's degree, a master's degree or a PhD in social work.
zh: 不分年龄、不分背景、遍及全国——哪里需要，社会工作者就到哪里帮忙。这行最广为人知的一面是充当社会安全网：我们引导人们获得关键资源，并在改变人生的抉择上提供咨询。全国有60多万名专业社会工作者，人人都有社会工作专业的学士、硕士或博士学位。

en: Stacey is going to walk you through the step-by-step process of becoming a social worker, and Mel will tell you about the range of options you have once you get your social work degree, as well as the high standards of responsibility the social workers must adhere to. The National Association of Social Workers represents nearly 145,000 social workers across the country. Our mission is to promote, protect and advance the social work profession.
zh: 斯泰西会带你一步步了解成为社会工作者的过程，梅尔则会告诉你拿到学位后有哪些选择，以及社会工作者必须恪守的高标准责任。全国社会工作者协会代表着全美近14.5万名社会工作者，我们的使命是推动、保护并发展社会工作这一专业。
